newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen rangebound ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen rangebound ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds will track sideways on Friday ahead of the release of U.S. producer price data at 1230 GMT, dealers said.
"We're all waiting for the data," one said. March PPI is seen unchanged on the month and slowing to a 1.8 percent year-on-year rate from 2.2 percent in February US-ECI.

It will be the first meaty piece of economic data the markets will have had the chance to get their teeth into since last Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls, which showed creeping wage inflation. Each piece of economic news is being scrutinised for what it might mean for U.S. interest rates.

Belgian OLOs edged lower on Thursday with other markets. The 10-year OLO yield was at around 6.03 percent at 1500 GMT, up from 5.97 late on Wednesday, while the spread over equivalent Bunds narrowed slightly to 11 from 12 basis points.

Dealers said in the absence of big flows, focus was on individual issues, such as the 6.75 percent May 1997 OLO 15 after a relatively modest exchange auction on Tuesday left the Treasury with 100 billion francs of the bond still outstanding and only one exchange auction left to try and mop it up.
One trader said OLO 15 was expensive relative to Treasury bills but clients holding it had said they would not sell.

"They say they are not holding it for the (exchange) option. They say they are just keeping it because all the paperwork and fees that are involved in selling doesn't make it worth their while," he said.

This would tend to suggest the Treasury will be forced to repay the outstanding principal and coupons when the bond expires on May 25. Before then, the issue features in just one exchange auction on May 13.
